outcome: No progress, partial result, or AI involvement was found for the generalized star-height problem since 26 January 2024; it remains open exactly as Wikipedia and the literature state.
summary: The generalized star-height problem (Brzozowski, 1980) asks whether every regular language can be described by a generalized regular expression (regular expressions plus complement) with bounded nesting depth of Kleene stars, and whether the minimum required depth is computable. It is a genuinely hard, narrow open problem: it is not even known whether a language of generalized star-height 2 exists (only height 0 and 1 are known to be realized). I checked the dedicated Wikipedia article 'Generalized star-height problem', which is a stub whose most recent citation is Sakarovitch (2009) and which was last touched only for routine maintenance (page last edited 2026-08-27, with no content change reflecting new research); the related 'Star height problem' article gives the same picture. I ran arXiv-focused searches (general and author-specific, e.g. for Tom Bourne and Nik Ruškuc, whose 2020-era work on Rees matrix semigroups and modular-subword languages is the most recent substantive progress I could locate, predating the window), checked the current cs.FL arXiv listing (16-22 September 2026) for any related submissions, and searched broadly for any claim of resolution, partial result, or AI-related work (including an AI-and-math angle) touching this problem. All searches turned up only pre-2024 material (1980s survey-era results through Bourne-Ruškuc's papers from the late 2010s/2020) or general encyclopedia pages restating the open status. One search result surfaced a GitHub repository under an org called 'vibemathing' titled 'problem-wikipedia-...: Vibe Mathing single-problem candidate research: Generalized star height problem' — this is evidently tooling/output from this same dataset-building effort (or a similar one), not an independent mathematical source, so I disregarded it per the instruction to work from primary sources only. No preprint, announcement, Lean/Coq formalization, or lab report addressing this problem in the 26 January 2024–22 September 2026 window was found. The triage's 'none' verdict is confirmed: this is a genuine case of 'nothing happened', and the record here documents that conclusion with the searches that support it.
competing_reading: None found. There is no genuine ambiguity here: no candidate result of any kind (resolution, case, bound, or AI-related incident) turned up in any search, so there is no alternative classification worth weighing.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or paper either (a) exhibiting a regular language of generalized star-height exactly 2 (settling the long-standing question of whether height >1 is ever needed), (b) proving no such language exists, or (c) giving an algorithm (or undecidability proof) for computing generalized star-height — together with expert digestion (e.g., citation/discussion in a survey, journal acceptance, or a specialist blog) confirming the argument holds up.
